Vide this judgment, this court shall dispose of complaint under section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act (hereinafter referred to as 'NI Act') filed by Sh. Vijender Kumar (hereinafter referred to as 'complainant') against Sh. Ajay Saini (hereinafter referred to as 'accused') for dishonour of cheque bearing number 000033 dated Digitally signed by CC No. 5914-2018 Page No.

2. Facts in brief as stated in the complaint are that complainant and accused were good friends .

In the first week of February 2015, accused had shown dire need of money and as per the friendly request of accused, complainant had arranged amount of Rs 6,00,000/- which was given to accused through cheque number 000004 drawn on HDFC Bank on 02.02.2015.
Accused promised that same would be returned before second week of August 2015.
It is stated that after receiving the aforesaid amount and execution of documents, accused paid Rs 20,000/- at end of 2015 as interest and failed to return the amount as promised by him.

It is stated that after eight months accused alongwith his father approached the complainant at his house and demanded Rs. 8,00,000/- for purchasing a property and complainant gave the said amount through cheque number 000024 amounting to Rs 5,00,000/- and cheque number 0000025 amounting to Rs 3,00,000/- on Vijendra Kr vs Ajay Saini on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27973642/
1 04.10.2016 and accused promised to return the same within one year.

After six months, accused against demanded Rs 3,00,000/- for urgent need and complainant issued cheque number 000035 for Rs.1,00,000/- dated 15.03.2017 and cheque number 074459 for Rs. 2,00,000/- dated 17.03.2017 and accused promised to return the entire amount with interest in month of November to complainant.
Digitally signed by 3.

It is stated that complainant approached the accused Shivangi Shivangi Vyas Vyas Date:
2024.10.09 17:57:39 +0530 for loan amount and interest after one year and accused issued cheque in question for part payment of loan amount and issued a promissory note in favor of complainant and stated that interest will be considered after payment of entire loan amount.
When complainant presented the said cheque, the same was returned with the remarks 'Funds Insufficient' vide returning memo dated 03.03.2018.

Thereafter, complainant has served a legal notice dated 31.03.2018 upon accused to make payment in respect of the aforesaid cheque within stipulated period of fifteen days and the said notice was served upon the accused on 03.04.2018.
Despite service accused failed to make payment and therefore the present complaint was filed.

4. Complainant tendered his pre-summoning evidence by way of affidavit EX CW1/X and relied upon following documents in his evidence :
Ex CW1/B : Original Cheque in question.

Ex CW1/E : Postal receipt alongwith tracking report (Ex. CW1/A which is stated to be copy of pass book of complainant is not filed on record during testimony)
5. Since prima facie offence under section 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act was made out, the accused was summoned vide order dated 28.06.2018.
Accused entered Shivangi Vyas his appearance and notice was served upon him for offence punishable u/s 138 NI Act on 07.01.2019, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

6. In his plea of defense, accused has submitted that the cheque in question was issued in favour of complainant and same bears his signature and contents in the same except the name of payee was filled by him.
He stated that he did not received any legal notice, however same bears his correct address.

He stated that he deposited amount of Rs.10,00,000/- on 30.11.2017 through NEFT no.
BARBX17334672724 in the account of Vijender Kumar Vats and thereafter an amount of Rs,5,00,000/- was withdrawn from his account on 01.12.2017 for payment of another installment towards his liability to Vijender Kumar Vats.

sentences.text: Shivangi Vyas 12.

Before adverting to scanning the evidence under the lens of the law pertaining to the lis at hand,
let us revisit the legal benchmark to be satisfied as enunciated in Section 138 of the Act.

Dishonour of Cheque for insufficiency, etc. of funds in the account: Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability, is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with that bank, such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence and shall, without prejudice to any other provision of this Act, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both.

Provided that nothing contained in this section shall apply unless-- (a) the cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier;
(b) the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, as the case may be, makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice in writing, to the drawer of the cheque,
[within thirty days] of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid; and (c) the drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money to the payee or as the case may be, to the holder in due course of the cheque within fifteen days of the Digitally signed by Shivangi Shivangi Vyas Vyas Date:
CC No. 5914-2018 Page No. 7 of 15 2024.10.09 17:58:30 +0530 receipt of the said notice.
Explanation.--For the purposes of this section, "debt or other liability" means a legally enforceable debt or other liability.
Vyas 14.

Being cumulative, it goes without saying that it is only when all the aforementioned ingredients are satisfied, the person who had drawn the cheque can be deemed to have committed an offence under Section 138 of the Act.
15. Averting to the facts of the present case, the cheque in question was admittedly signed by accused as he has admitted his signature on the cheque in question.
The presentation and dishonor of cheque is depicted by cheque return memo Ex CW1/C which shows the reason for dishonor as 'Funds Insufficient'.
The complainant has deposed that cheque was returned dishonored due to the said reason and the accused has also not disputed the dishonor of cheque for the above reason or the cheque return memo.
16. Once the execution of cheque is admitted by accused, statutory rebuttable presumptions under section 118(a) and 139 NI Act arise in favour of complainant and against accused.

Section 118 of the Act inter alia provides the presumptions as to negotiable instruments that until the contrary is proved, the presumption shall be made that every negotiable instrument was made or drawn for consideration, and that every such instrument, when it has been accepted, endorsed, negotiated or transferred was accepted, endorsed, negotiated or transferred for consideration.

Further, section 139 of the Act provides that it shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the Shivangi Vyas CC No. 5914-2018 Page No. 9 of 15 by Shivangi Vyas holder of a cheque received the cheque of the nature referred to in Section 138 for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability.
17.

It is clear from the conjoint reading of both the provisions that ordinarily in the cheque dishonor cases, what the courts ought to consider is whether the ingredients of the offence enumerated in Section 138 of the Act have been met and if so, whether the accused was able to rebut the statutory presumption contemplated by Section 139 of the Act.

sentences.text: Further, the standard of proof required to rebut the presumption raised under S.118 and 139 of the Act is only that of 'preponderance of probabilities' and therefore, the accused is required to prove only a probable defence of non-existence of liability and is not required to establish the same beyond reasonable doubt.
The accused must do so by either adducing his own evidence or by punching holes in the case of the complainant through cross examination of complainant.
19. The defence of accused is that he had issued the cheque in November,2017 and has already made the payment to complainant through RTGS and through cash withdrawn from the bank.
Complainant in his cross- examination has claimed that accused borrowed money from him from 2014 to 2017.

He deposed that accused borrowed Rs.2,00,000/- per month from him for one year as Digitally signed by Shivangi Shivangi Vyas Vyas Date:
2024.10.09 17:58:58 +0530 installment of Matka committee in the year 2016 and promised to return Rs.30,00,000/- which included Rs.24,00,000/- principal amount and Rs.3,00,000/- as interest for one year which he did not return.
He further deposed that accused had borrowed Rs.15,00,000/- and Rs.12,00,000/- from him for other committees during the year 2014-2015.
He deposed that accused has also started four other committees of Rs. 6,00,000/- each and did not return any amount out of the said four committees.
Complainant admitted that he did not disclose aforesaid amount borrowed from him in his complaint.
20. From the testimony of complainant it is apparent that hefty amount of money has been continuously paid to the accused in the name of one committee or other without any security.
The complainant claimed that he had given the said amount in cash as he has sold his property.
The transaction of aforesaid loan amounts given in cash without any security and that too only for the purpose of investment by accused in committee seems extravagant and rather unbelievable.
No prudent person would continue advancing loan of such huge amounts for mere investment by accused in committee specially so when the prior amount is not paid before advancing further loan amount.

21. Further, complainant has claimed that an agreement and a pro note was executed in his favour but he failed to file those documents on record despite being questioned Shivangi Vyas CC No.
5914-2018 Page No. 11 of 15 Date: 2024.10.09 about them.
There is no document filed by complainant to substantiate his claim of prior transactions between the parties.
The complainant has further admitted that he did not disclose any of the loan transactions in his ITR.
The complainant has allegedly given multiple loans of huge amount running into lakhs to the accused but none of those loan amount is disclosed in his ITR.
Complainant has claimed that he had the amount as he sold his property but failed to disclose the value of sale consideration or any other details of property.

The court is mindful of fact that non-disclosure of loan amount does not affect the validity of loan transaction per se although the same may attract liability under relevant penal laws, but the non-disclosure in Income Tax Returns raise doubt regarding the transaction of loan itself.

Also, the complainant has admitted that he did not have license to lend money on interest and he has allegedly given loan on multiple occasions on interest which compounded to be Rs.
80,00,000/-.
The complainant without any license gave such huge amount as loan to accused and that too the major portion of loan was given for investment in committee.
Also, there is another aspect of the transfer of property by father of accused to the complainant which has been put across by accused as discharge of liability of repayment of loan.
The validity or not of the said transaction is not the subject matter of present complaint and the same has not been dealt with.

Digitally signed by Shivangi Shivangi Vyas Vyas Date:
2024.10.09 17:59:22 +0530
Nevertheless, the said property is also stated to be in possession of complainant and purportedly sold to a third party which has emerged from the testimony of complainant.
The complainant has also admitted having possession of multiple cheques of accused some of those are stated to be stale.
23. The accused has admitted receiving the amount of Rupees Sixteen Lacs from complainant but has claimed that said amount is already returned to the complainant.
Complainant admitted the return of amount through NEFT but stated that the same pertain to prior transaction between parties as he had to recover Rs 80,00,000/- from accused.
The said amount purportedly stems from the prior loan transactions as enumerated by complainant in his testimony but those transactions themselves appear to be doubtful.

Through the cross examination of complainant, wherein he himself admitted receiving the amount of Rs 17,00,000/- from accused, accused has been successful in raising the doubt regarding the pending liability of repayment of loan amount which was to be repaid in November 2017.
Out of the said amount Rs. 10,00,000/- has been admittedly paid through NEFT in November 2017.

While the complainant claimed that said payment pertains to other separate transactions, none of those transactions, as per the version of complainant himself,
entailed repayment in November 2017.

Therefore, the complainant failed to establish the pendency of liability of accused to repay the loan amount of Digitally signed by Shivangi Shivangi Vyas Vyas Date:
2024.10.09 17:59:31 +0530 Rupees Seventeen Lakh for which cheque in question is allegedly issued in December, 2017.
24. Another defence taken by accused is that the legal demand notice has not been received by him.
The delivery of legal demand notice dated 31.03.2018 Ex CW1/D is reflected from the postal receipt and tracking report Ex CW1/E.

Further, the accused himself has admitted the delivery of legal notice and the documents EX CW1/D and Ex CW1/E when the same were put to him while recording his statement under section 313 CrPC on 02.02.2023.

While the delivery of legal notice is established,
the legal notice Ex CW1/D itself appears to be invalid.
The relevant paragraph of legal notice regarding the demand made to the accused has been reproduced here:

"Now, through the medium of this notice to you, the addressee are thereby call upon you to make the payment of entire loan amount of Rs. 15,00,000(Rs. Five Lac only)
and by way of this notice you the addressee pay Rs. 5,00,000/- alongwith interest of 24% per annum to my client within 15 days from the ate of receipt of this notice, I Vijendra Kr vs Ajay Saini on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27973642/
7 had instructions from my client in case payment is not made by you to my client within 15 days from the date of receipt of this notice, my client shall be compelled to file complaint against you under section U/s 138 N.I. Act and U/s 420 of IPC and file civil suit under 037 CPC and also filed and suit for Possession in the court of law Shivangi Vyas CC No. 5914-2018 Page No. 14 of 15 17:59:42 +0530 having jurisdiction in the matter at your risks and costs".
25.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The notice Ex CW1/D demands the entire loan amount which is Rupees Seventeen Lac and which is wrongly mentioned as Rupees Fifteen Lac in figures and Rupees Five Lac in words in the notice.
Further, Rupees Five Lac in figures are again demanded along with interest at rate of 24 percent per anum by way of notice.
The language of notice is incomprehensible and the exact amount demanded by way of notice is unclear.

The demand of the cheque amount has to made in clear terms through the legal notice affording an opportunity to the other party to clear the amount of dishonored cheque which was not done so in the present case.

26. From the above discussion, it can be concluded that the complainant has failed to establish the necessary ingredient of existence of legal liability and service of valid legal notice upon accused which are essential for offence under section 138 NI Act.
Consequently, this court finds the accused Ajay Saini not guilty of offence under section 138, Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 and acquits him accordingly.
